questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The avaibility to explore Paris and learn the French culture and language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was okay. I received e-mails with info from KU and the host university via E-mail. But there was also a lot of information and things you need to find out yourself after arrival. 
I had some questions regarding the documents we needed to fill out, but the host university replied after some time so I could fill all the documents correct.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was some welcome days where the Erasmus students received information and saw the university. 
We all got a french student as a "buddy". So you could always ask that person questions. 
The school employees was sweet to say where and who you can ask about stuff, but it is not always efficient so you need to have patience regarding information and student cards etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
This was beforehand one of the trickiest things. 
I was unsure whether I wanted to live in Cergy near the University, in Paris or in between the cities. 
I chose to live in Paris with the other student from Jura on KU that was going on an exchange too. 
Together we found an apartment through Air bnb. Firstly we searched a lot of apartments through facebook groups, but with the amount of scams it was hard to know who and what was not scam. Therefore we chose to be safe and book through Air bnb. 
We found an apartment in the 2nd arrondissement. We payed around 6800 kr. per person every month. 
It took around 45 minutes to get to the University since we lived close to the RER A train station which goes to Cergy station.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I recommend everyone to live in Paris instead of Cergy. 
During the introduction days we were several times told to be carefull going to the station in Cergy at night since it is not one of the safest places, but there is no problems there during the daytime. 
I only had classes on 3 weekdays why I therefore could spent more days in Paris than at the University. 
The other Erasmus students from other countries all lived nearer to the University but they all regret not staying in Paris. They did not think it was a possibility before they saw that we did it. So instead they ended up being the ones using the train more to go to Paris and therefore they sometimes had to use money on Ubers to get back to Cergy and also because the trains did not go so often after midnight if we were out in Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They recommended you to find it on your own but I know they helped the ones who hadn´t found housing before arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very old system. It was easy enough to write to the person in charge of the legal department about your wished course registrations. But after that you need to register in person in different offices to know when and at what time your classes will be.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask for help at the offices but not everyone was good at french.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and they were kind to help with making sure you got classes that did not collide timewise.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again, be patience with the informations and their system in France. It is not efficient but everything will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had both Bachelor (they call it Licence), Masters and LLM courses. 
The level was most easy on the licence and then moving up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The courses in the different programs have very different teaching style from Copenhagen. 
Some courses they call TD´s which are like seminars in Denmark in a classroom. In most of those couses part of your grade will reflect on participation in class (like 10-20%). But don´t be afraid of that. It´s not that difficult to pass the courses compared to in Copenhagen. 
Some other courses are CM´s which are like lectures in Denmark. These courses will end with a final examination.

I never had to prepare for any classes since there was no books. So everything the teacher say or the powerpoints is what you focus on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Torts (TD) - 3 ECTS 
Corporate Law (TD) - 3 ECTS
Writing contracts (TD) - 3 ECTS 
Business Law (CM) - 6 ECTS 
Intellectual Property (LLM) - 8 ECTS 
Company Law (LLM) - 8 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked all my courses. My least favorite was Business Law because the professor spoke with a big french accent. 
In many of my other courses the teachers spoke very good english. Some of them were from english speaking countries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The ELSA organization organize different days and afternoons with activities for the Erasmus students doing Law. 
I didnt but I thought about joining the sports club. 
I registered for the French course to learn some French.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not sure. But hang out with the other erasmus students to do non-academic activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore Paris and other cities nearby. 
Together with the other Erasmus students I went to Normandie and Bordeaux including wine tasting. I thought about going to Champagne area and other cities as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
You can contact your "buddy" to socialize with french local students and the Elsa Organization which also host some different acti. 
You can also socialize with the french students from your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The slow and inefficient systems in France.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that it is so easy to find a cute café to sit and drink coffee and have a croissant. And just the whole vibe in Paris is amazing. The city is so beautiful everywhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Live in Paris and get a monthly Navigo travel pass so you can get around easily in Paris and back and forth from University
2. Be patient with the French way of organizing and structuring courses, classes and more. 
3. Socialize with the other Erasmus students in the introduction days. We became a big group of friends from the first days that hang out a lot.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I had never had French lessons before but I got around fine. But it will be a advantage and much easier to speak with natives if you know some more French.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience of exploring Paris streets, culture, food and wine. I got a lot of friends from all over Europe too.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be more independent by seeking information and exploring.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
